description: Deterministic rule seed for future L5.3 event and state-change normalization. This layer defines catalogs and validation rules only.

review_decision_enum.meaning: human reviewer accepts this candidate as usable for future normalization
human reviewer marks this candidate as duplicate or mergeable
human reviewer marks this candidate as containing multiple events
candidate requires more surrounding evidence before decision
candidate is plausible but not reliable enough

event_type_catalog.description: A character or entity changes position or presence.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not infer exact origin or destination if candidates are absent.

event_type_catalog.description: Two or more entities meet or perceive each other in a scene.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Requires evidence that the encounter occurs in the candidate span.

event_type_catalog.description: Speech, command, negotiation, warning, or announcement.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Dialogue content is not truth until reviewed against evidence.

event_type_catalog.description: A dispute or clash that may be verbal, physical, ideological, internal, or group-based.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Use battle for large-scale organized conflict.

event_type_catalog.description: An agent attempts or performs harm against a target.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not infer attack success unless evidence states it.

event_type_catalog.description: An entity blocks, protects, shields, rescues, or suppresses harm.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Defense can coexist with attack but must not be auto-merged.

event_type_catalog.description: A character or entity becomes harmed, weakened, unconscious, or damaged.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not promote to death unless death evidence exists.

event_type_catalog.description: A character or entity dies or is destroyed in a life-state sense.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Death is high-impact and must retain explicit evidence.

event_type_catalog.description: A dead, near-dead, dormant, or unconscious entity revives.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Separate true resurrection from ordinary recovery during review.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject is restrained, imprisoned, sealed, or taken by force.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Capture does not imply later custody state without evidence.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject flees or breaks out of danger, confinement, or pursuit.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Escape may be a movement subtype, but remains separate when captivity is present.

event_type_catalog.description: An entity searches, tracks, probes, or investigates a target.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Search is distinct from discovery; success requires discovery evidence.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject finds or notices an entity, place, fact, object, or clue.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Discovery changes knowledge, not necessarily the discovered entity.

event_type_catalog.description: Information, identity, rule, relationship, or hidden fact is revealed.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Treat revealed content as a claim until review confirms evidence.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject chooses a plan, action, stance, route, or judgment.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Intent is not execution; keep decision separate from later action.

event_type_catalog.description: A character promises, swears, vows, or makes a binding statement.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Promise content is captured as evidence, not executed.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject breaks loyalty, exposes an ally, or acts against a trusted party.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Requires explicit evidence of trust or affiliation being violated.

event_type_catalog.description: Two or more entities form, maintain, or declare cooperation.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Alliance requires evidence of cooperation, not just shared location.

event_type_catalog.description: Characters, groups, or entities separate physically, socially, or narratively.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Separate from betrayal unless hostile intent is present.

event_type_catalog.description: Previously separated entities meet again.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Requires prior or implied separation only as review context, not inference.

event_type_catalog.description: A character's identity, name, role, or recognized status changes.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Keep distinct from disguise or impersonation.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject hides, masks, imitates, or performs another identity.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Disguise can support performance but must not imply true identity change.

event_type_catalog.description: A power, skill, domain effect, or supernatural ability is used.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Usage does not imply power upgrade.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject gains, upgrades, awakens, loses, or changes power level.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Future normalization must distinguish awakening, usage, and level change.

event_type_catalog.description: A formal ritual, sacrifice, invocation, sealing, or ceremonial act occurs.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not infer ritual result unless explicit.

event_type_catalog.description: A theatrical, staged, role-based, mask, or audience-facing action occurs.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Kept for 戏神道, performance, stage, disguise, and role-play related events.

event_type_catalog.description: An organization meets, acts, exposes itself, attacks, collapses, or changes structure.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Organization statements need explicit evidence and entity review.

event_type_catalog.description: A mission, order, request, assignment, or operational task is created or changed.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Assignment is distinct from mission completion.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject systematically investigates a person, event, place, clue, or rule.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Use discovery or reveal when information is actually found.

event_type_catalog.description: An authority judges, sentences, condemns, clears, or decides a case.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Judgment does not imply sentence execution.

event_type_catalog.description: A world rule, domain boundary, godway principle, disaster law, or setting-level rule shifts.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Kept for rules, boundaries, red star, godway, and disaster shifts.

event_type_catalog.description: A disaster, gray tide, gray world, contamination, mutation, or annihilation event occurs.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Kept for 灾厄, 灰界, 灰潮, contamination, and suppression.

event_type_catalog.description: A hostile force, disaster, organization, or entity enters territory or domain.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Use disaster_event if the main evidence is disaster behavior.

event_type_catalog.description: A large-scale or named fight involving multiple actions or organized sides.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Individual attacks may remain separate candidates until reviewed.

event_type_catalog.description: Narrative moves to a new scene, time, place, or viewpoint.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Minor by default unless tied to major plot change.

event_type_catalog.description: A character's emotional, mental, or internal condition changes.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Avoid converting every thought into a major event.

event_type_catalog.description: An object, artifact, weapon, token, or evidence item is obtained, lost, destroyed, or transferred.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Object ownership needs an object candidate or reviewed evidence.

event_type_catalog.description: A resource, currency, material, life force, power reserve, or count changes.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not calculate amounts if text does not provide them.

event_type_catalog.description: A subject learns, forgets, understands, misunderstands, or receives information.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Many reveal and discovery events also create knowledge changes.

event_type_catalog.description: The relationship between entities changes.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not infer relationship labels from proximity alone.

event_type_catalog.description: A safe generic event type for reviewed but not yet specific state/status changes.
event_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Safe fallback for unknown trigger categories.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Entity location or spatial relationship changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Unknown endpoints remain empty until reviewed.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Identity, name, role, or recognized status changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not infer canonical identity without reviewed entity mapping.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Disguise, mask, alias, impersonation, or role state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Disguise is not final identity.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Relationship state changes between two entities.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Requires explicit evidence or review decision.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Health, wound, damage, or consciousness state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not convert injury into death without death evidence.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Alive/dead or destroyed state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: High-impact state change requiring explicit evidence.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Dead, dormant, unconscious, or disabled state changes toward revival or recovery.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Separate revival from ordinary healing when possible.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Power presence, skill state, ability state, or usage state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Usage and acquisition are separate review concepts.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Rank, stage, realm, or power level changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Never invent level names.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Membership or affiliation in an organization changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Review organization identity before canonicalizing.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Authority, command, rank, judgment, or authorization changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Authority claims are evidence-bound.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Known, unknown, understood, revealed, or suspected state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Knowledge may belong to observer, speaker, or subject.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Emotional state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Minor by default unless explicit and plot-critical.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Mental, intent, memory, or resolve state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Avoid over-indexing generic narration.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Ownership or possession of an object changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Object and owner candidates require review.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Resource amount, status, or availability changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not compute quantities.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Mission or objective state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Assigned, active, complete, failed, or canceled require evidence.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Captivity, confinement, restraint, or release state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Confinement state should be manually reviewed.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Alliance state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Temporary cooperation and formal alliance are separate review outcomes.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Hostility, enmity, conflict, or threat state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Hostility requires explicit hostile action or statement.

state_change_type_catalog.description: World rule, boundary, godway, or domain rule changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not infer setting laws without evidence.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Scene, domain, disaster, weather-like, or environment state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Environment change may be local or world-level.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Disaster manifestation, contamination, suppression, or defeat state changes.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Disaster entities require review before canonical mapping.

state_change_type_catalog.description: An entity becomes present or absent in a scene.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Derived scene presence must stay candidate-only until L5.3.

state_change_type_catalog.description: Generic status change not yet classified more specifically.
state_change_type_catalog.normalization_notes: Generic fallback for safe future normalization.

argument_role_catalog.description: Primary entity involved in the event.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Use unknown if no reviewed subject exists.

argument_role_catalog.description: Secondary entity, statement, task, or thing involved.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Object is generic; prefer target, patient, or artifact when known.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity, place, or group targeted by an action.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not invent target if text only has an action.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity that performs an action.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Agent may be unknown for passive evidence.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity affected by injury, death, revival, capture, or judgment.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Patient is distinct from target when harm result is explicit.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity that speaks or communicates.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Speaker may be absent in indirect narration.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity receiving speech or communication.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Listener can be group or unknown.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity that witnesses, observes, or becomes aware.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Observation changes knowledge only after review.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity that finds or notices something.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Required for discovery if available.

argument_role_catalog.description: Fact, entity, identity, rule, or clue revealed or discovered.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: May remain raw candidate until reviewed.

argument_role_catalog.description: Entity that moves or changes presence.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Movement can involve disaster or organization as entity.

argument_role_catalog.description: Location before movement or transfer.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Leave empty if not explicit.

argument_role_catalog.description: Location after movement or transfer.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Leave empty if not explicit.

argument_role_catalog.description: Location or scene where the event occurs.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: May be scene-derived later, not in L5.2.

argument_role_catalog.description: Narrative or story-time hint.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Time hints are not canonical timeline positions.

argument_role_catalog.description: Organization directly involved.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Requires organization review for canonical IDs.

argument_role_catalog.description: Side, faction, group, or alliance position.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Do not invent faction labels.

argument_role_catalog.description: Power system entity involved.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Power references require reviewed seed/catalog mapping.

argument_role_catalog.description: Specific ability or skill used.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Ability can remain raw text.

argument_role_catalog.description: Object or artifact involved.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: No automatic artifact resolution.

argument_role_catalog.description: Weapon used in attack or defense.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Weapon can be raw object candidate.

argument_role_catalog.description: Resource that changes or is consumed.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: No numeric inference.

argument_role_catalog.description: Cause or trigger behind an event.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Causal claims need evidence.

argument_role_catalog.description: Result or outcome indicated by evidence.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Result should stay textual until normalized later.

argument_role_catalog.description: Method, mechanism, or manner of action.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: No hidden method inference.

argument_role_catalog.description: Evidence text or evidence anchor.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Future normalized rows must retain evidence coordinates and hash.

argument_role_catalog.description: Scene block or narrative scene.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Scene source is optional in L5.0/L5.1 and must not be invented.

argument_role_catalog.description: Chapter anchor for the candidate.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Chapter is an anchor, not a story-time fact.

argument_role_catalog.description: Placeholder role when a candidate lacks a reliable argument role.
argument_role_catalog.normalization_notes: Use only as explicit uncertainty marker.

trigger_category_mapping.notes: Location-triggered candidates usually normalize as movement or scene transition.
Explicit safe fallback for unknown categories.
L5.0 family; event_type_candidate mapping refines it later.

l5_state_change_type_candidate_mapping.notes: Review decides injury, death, or revival.

confidence_rules.description: Boost when trigger text and evidence span are both present and back-cut valid.
Boost when a subject or mover-like candidate exists.
Boost when an object, target, patient, or revealed entity candidate exists.
Boost when a location or scene candidate exists.
Boost when an event candidate has a linked state-change candidate.
Boost when evidence hash and offset back-cut validate.
Penalty for likely duplicate trigger or evidence candidates.
Penalty when evidence span is absent.
Penalty when required argument candidates are absent.
Penalty for weak or generic triggers.
Penalty when scene block reference is invalid.
Boost for future reviewed accept decision.
Hard confidence suppression for future reviewed reject decision.
Penalty when a reviewer marks the candidate as needing more context.

importance_rules.description: Death and revival candidates are major or critical plot events.
Power upgrades are major by default.
Identity changes are major by default.
Disaster events are major by default.
Relationship changes are normal unless supported by major context.
Organization membership changes are normal by default.
Core information reveal candidates are major when reviewed.
Dialogue is normal unless another rule upgrades it.
Internal state changes are minor by default.

merge_key_rules.description: Future grouping may place same sentence and trigger candidates in one review group.
merge_key_rules.notes: Does not auto-confirm or delete candidates.

merge_key_rules.description: Future grouping may place same evidence hash and trigger candidates in one review group.
merge_key_rules.notes: Group only; no automatic event fact.

merge_key_rules.description: Future grouping may group same scene, subject, and canonical type candidates for review.
merge_key_rules.notes: Manual review required before any merge outcome.

merge_key_rules.description: Future state-change candidates may be linked to a reviewed event record.
merge_key_rules.notes: Defines linking behavior only; source rows remain unchanged.

merge_key_rules.description: No merge is allowed without review or an explicit future deterministic acceptance rule.
merge_key_rules.notes: Prevents automatic confirmation or silent de-duplication.

reject_rules.description: Future candidate should be unusable for normalization if no evidence exists.
reject_rules.notes: Does not delete data or mutate source tables.

reject_rules.description: Future candidate should be rejected if evidence offsets are invalid.
Future candidate should be rejected if evidence hash does not match back-cut text.
Future candidate should be rejected if trigger text is empty.
Future candidate should be rejected if source chapter anchor is missing.
Human rejected candidates should not normalize into final facts.
Descriptions that are not actual event/state candidates should be excluded in future normalization.
reject_rules.notes: Manual-only because semantic judgment is required.

reject_rules.description: Duplicate noise may be marked unusable after review.
reject_rules.notes: Soft reject only; duplicate grouping must not delete rows.

downgrade_rules.description: Downgrade when subject-like argument is missing.
Downgrade when object or target is required but missing.
downgrade_rules.notes: Applies to attack, transfer, reveal, and relationship candidates.

downgrade_rules.description: Downgrade movement candidates missing location evidence.
downgrade_rules.notes: Movement can still be valid with only mover evidence after review.

downgrade_rules.description: Downgrade when scene block is unavailable or missing.
downgrade_rules.notes: Scene source is optional in current L5.0/L5.1.

downgrade_rules.description: Downgrade candidates with multiple evidence spans pending review.
Downgrade only mildly when optional location or scene sources are missing.
downgrade_rules.notes: Optional missing sources should not fail default verification.

warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Reject or request regeneration with evidence.
Review whether split or merge is needed.
Reject unless source can be audited.
Mark needs_context or review evidence.
Review surrounding evidence.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Object or target candidate is missing.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Review if object is required for this type.
Review movement or scene context.
Keep candidate; scene source may be optional.
Check scene source compatibility.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Evidence back-cut status is not ok.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Reject or repair source coordinates in a later layer.
Reject for future normalization.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Candidate trigger is weak or generic.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Downgrade unless review accepts it.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Duplicate trigger appears in the same sentence.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Group for review; do not auto-merge.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Duplicate event candidate appears to share evidence.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Group for review; do not auto-merge.

warning_flag_catalog.description: State-change candidate lacks a linked event.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Review linkage.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Event candidate has no linked state-change candidate.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Acceptable for many event types.
Keep candidate and note coverage gap.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Optional scene block source is missing.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Keep candidate and note coverage gap.
Do not normalize into final facts.
Keep candidate out of confirmed outputs.
Keep candidate out of confirmed outputs unless later accepted.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Candidate violates L5.2 guardrails for normalization.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Do not normalize.

warning_flag_catalog.description: Manual review is required before future normalization or grouping.
warning_flag_catalog.recommended_action: Route to review queue.

normalization_guardrails.description: Candidate rows must not be treated as confirmed story facts.
Future confirmed event generation requires review_decision or equivalent deterministic acceptance criteria.
Character/location/organization normalization must not be invented from text alone.
A future normalized event must retain evidence coordinates and evidence hash.
L1/L2/L3/L4/L5.0 source tables must remain read-only.

future_tables.description: Future table for reviewed and normalized event records.
Future table for reviewed and normalized state change records.
Future table for deterministic candidate grouping or human-reviewed merge groups.
